b.answer:
Worked example: tidying names on Harvest Lane's Orders rows before they reach the Customers sheet.

Code node, JavaScript, mode Run Once for Each Item:

// Run Once for Each Item
const raw = String($json.name ?? '');   // ?? '' stops "undefined" appearing
const name = raw
  .trim()                               // drop spaces at both ends
  .replace(/\s+/g, ' ')                 // double spaces become one
  .toLowerCase()                        // "CHEF TUNDE" -> "chef tunde"
  .replace(/\b\w/g, ch => ch.toUpperCase()); // capitalise each word
return { json: { ...$json, name, name_missing: name === '' } };
Input nameOutput namename_missing
" mrs adebayo "Mrs Adebayofalse
"CHEF TUNDE"Chef Tundefalse
"iya basira" (two spaces)Iya Basirafalse
"" (or no name field)"" (empty)true

Why it works: ...$json copies every other field (order_id, phone, total) unchanged, and only name is overwritten. The ?? '' matters: String(undefined) is the word "undefined", which would then be capitalised into a customer called Undefined. The name_missing flag lets an IF downstream send blank names to the Fix list.

Evidence: the Output panel in Table view with all four test items and their other fields still present.
mistakes: Returning only { json: { name } }, which throws away order_id, phone and total.
Using String($json.name) without a fallback, so a missing name becomes "Undefined".
Writing all-items code ($input.all() and an array return) in each-item mode.
Collapsing only leading and trailing spaces, so "iya  basira" keeps its double space.
b.pass: All four test names come out as shown (Title Case, single spaces, empty stays empty without an error), and every other field is still on each output item.
b.redo: Send it back if the node errors on the empty name, any other field is lost, or the mode is wrong.

s.answer:
Worked example: a week of Harvest Lane order lines (product, qty, line_total, order_id). Eight lines: tomatoes in HL-1, HL-2 and HL-5; pepper in HL-1 and HL-4; ugwu in HL-3 and HL-5; onions in HL-6. One line_total arrives as the text "45000".

// Run Once for All Items
const byProduct = {};
for (const { json: o } of $input.all()) {
  const p = byProduct[o.product] ??= { product: o.product, qty: 0, revenue: 0, orders: new Set() };
  p.qty += Number(o.qty) || 0;
  p.revenue += Number(o.line_total) || 0;
  p.orders.add(o.order_id);            // count each order once
}
const rows = Object.values(byProduct);
const grand = rows.reduce((s, p) => s + p.revenue, 0);
return rows
  .sort((a, b) => b.revenue - a.revenue)
  .map(p => ({ json: {
    product: p.product,
    total_qty: p.qty,
    total_revenue: p.revenue,
    orders: p.orders.size,
    avg_order_value: Math.round(p.revenue / p.orders.size),
    share_of_revenue: Math.round(p.revenue / grand * 1000) / 10,
  } }));
producttotal_qtytotal_revenueordersavg_order_valueshare_of_revenue
Tomatoes (basket)6₦90,0003₦30,00059.6
Pepper (bag)3₦36,0002₦18,00023.8
Onions (bag)1₦18,0001₦18,00011.9
Ugwu (bundle)14₦7,0002₦3,5004.6

Checks: in the sheet, =SUMIF(A:A,"Tomatoes (basket)",C:C) gives 90000, and the same for each product; the four revenues add to ₦151,000. Shares add to 99.9%, which is rounding, not an error.

Notes: the Set counts an order once even if it has two tomato lines. A Set can't be returned as JSON, so the code returns its .size. Rounding happens only at the end, for display.
mistakes: Adding line_total without Number(), so one text value turns a sum into a long string.
Counting order lines instead of distinct orders, which inflates orders and lowers the average.
Rounding each line before summing, so totals drift away from the SUMIF.
Returning the Set or a plain number list instead of [{ json: {...} }] items.
s.pass: One item per product sorted by revenue, each revenue equal to a SUMIF on the same data, and share_of_revenue values that add to 100% within rounding.
s.redo: Send it back if any revenue differs from the SUMIF, the sort is wrong, or shares are missing or don't add up.

Worked example: Harvest Lane's "at-risk customers" flag, drafted by an AI from the Card 5 prompt and audited with fake data.

// AI first draft (excerpt)
const today = new Date();
for (const item of $input.all()) {
  const o = item.json;
  c = customers[o.phone] || { orders: 0, last: o.date };
  c.orders += 1;
  if (new Date(o.date) > new Date(c.last)) c.last = o.date;
  ...
}
Predicted edge caseTest itemDraft result
Phone formatsMrs Adebayo as 0803 123 4567 and +2348031234567Failed: counted as two customers with one order each, so not flagged
Odd date format14/09/2026Failed: new Date read it as Invalid Date, so the last order was wrong
Missing phoneOrder with phone ""Failed: all blank phones grouped as one "customer"

Final code (with today as 5 October, the cutoff is 21 August):

const normPhone = p => {                 // same rule as the solved problem
  const d = String(p ?? '').replace(/\D/g, '');
  if (!d) return null;
  return d.startsWith('234') ? '+' + d : '+234' + d.replace(/^0/, '');
};
const toISO = d => {                     // accept 2026-09-14 or 14/09/2026
  const s = String(d ?? '').trim();
  let dt = DateTime.fromISO(s);
  if (!dt.isValid) dt = DateTime.fromFormat(s, 'dd/MM/yyyy');
  return dt.isValid ? dt.toISODate() : null;
};
const cutoff = $today.minus({ days: 45 }).toISODate();
const byPhone = {};
for (const { json: o } of $input.all()) {
  const phone = normPhone(o.phone), date = toISO(o.date);
  if (!phone || !date) continue;         // the IF before this node logs these
  const c = byPhone[phone] ??= { phone, name: String(o.name).trim(), orders: 0, last_order: date };
  c.orders += 1;
  if (date > c.last_order) c.last_order = date;
}
return Object.values(byPhone)
  .filter(c => c.orders >= 2 && c.last_order < cutoff)
  .map(c => ({ json: { ...c, at_risk: true } }));

Log to submit: the AI's draft, the three-row test table above with "draft" and "final" results, the final code with a comment on each line in your own words, and the output: for example, Mr Okafor (3 orders, last 2026-08-02) flagged; Chef Tunde (last 2026-09-28) not flagged.
mistakes: Testing the AI's code only on the clean sample it was given, so no bug is ever found.
Pasting real customer names and phones into the AI chat.
Leaving "explain each line" to the AI's own comments instead of writing them in your own words.
Hard-coding today's date, so the flag is wrong from tomorrow on.
g.pass: The log shows the AI's first draft, at least one failing test case and what failed, and final code that passes all predicted edge cases with every line explained in the learner's words.
g.redo: Send it back if no bug was found or recorded, real data was used, or the explanations are copied rather than the learner's own.
